ground_truth.description: SQL Injection in login endpoint - username and password directly concatenated into SQL query without parameterization
JWT Algorithm Confusion attack possible - algorithm taken from user-controlled X-JWT-Alg header without validation
IDOR vulnerability - any authenticated user can access any other user's profile by changing user_id in URL
SQL Injection in transactions listing endpoint - multiple parameters (user_id, limit, offset, sort_by, order) directly concatenated into SQL query
SSRF vulnerability in webhook handler - callback_url from request body used directly to make server-side requests without validation or allowlisting
Path Traversal in file download - filename from user input joined with base path without sanitization, allowing directory traversal attacks (e.g., ../../../etc/passwd)
Unrestricted File Upload - original filename preserved without validation of extension or content type, allowing upload of malicious files
OS Command Injection in admin backup endpoint - backup_type and output_path parameters concatenated into shell command without sanitization
Hardcoded credentials exposed via config export endpoint - database passwords, API keys, encryption keys all returned in plaintext
Insecure Deserialization in config import - pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows remote code execution
Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) - user-provided template string rendered with Jinja2 without sandboxing or restrictions
Reflected XSS in search endpoint - user query directly inserted into HTML response without encoding or sanitization
Open Redirect - next parameter from query string used in redirect without validation against allowlist
SSRF in internal proxy endpoint - url parameter or service name used to make internal network requests without restriction
